description: Held-out set of 40 vague, non-technical business questions against the bench database (data ends 2026-10-10). Written independently of the retrieval code and of large_tasks.json. needed_relations is the minimal set a competent analyst would read; each ground-truth query uses exactly those relations.

tasks.name: biggest_customers_2026
tasks.question: Who were our 10 biggest customers in 2026 so far?

queries.name: top_customers_2026
queries.sql: select c.customer_name, round(sum(o.total_usd), 2) as revenue_usd from sales.orders o join sales.customers c on c.cust_id = o.cust_id where o.order_dt >= '2026-01-01' and o.order_dt < '2026-10-11' and o.status not in ('cancelled', 'draft') group by c.customer_name order by revenue_usd desc limit 10

tasks.name: sales_trend_monthly
tasks.question: How have sales been trending month to month since October 2025?

queries.name: monthly_sales
queries.sql: select date_trunc('month', order_dt)::date as month, count(*) as orders, round(sum(total_usd), 2) as revenue_usd from sales.orders where order_dt >= '2025-10-01' and order_dt < '2026-10-11' and status not in ('cancelled', 'draft') group by 1 order by 1 limit 13

tasks.name: flying_off_shelves
tasks.question: What stuff is flying off the shelves the most?

queries.name: best_selling_products
queries.sql: select p.sku, p.product_name, sum(oi.qty) as units_sold from sales.order_items oi join inventory.products p on p.product_id = oi.product_id group by p.sku, p.product_name order by units_sold desc limit 10

tasks.name: reps_crushing_it
tasks.question: Which of our sales reps are crushing it this year?

queries.name: rep_leaderboard_2026
queries.sql: select e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, count(*) as orders, round(sum(o.total_usd), 2) as revenue_usd from sales.orders o join hr.employees e on e.employee_id = o.sales_rep_id where o.order_dt >= '2026-01-01' and o.order_dt < '2026-10-11' and o.status not in ('cancelled', 'draft') group by e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name order by revenue_usd desc limit 10

tasks.name: why_things_come_back
tasks.question: Why do people keep sending stuff back to us?

queries.name: return_reasons
queries.sql: select reason, count(*) as returns, sum(qty) as units, round(sum(refund_amt), 2) as refunded from sales.returns group by reason order by returns desc limit 10

tasks.name: who_owes_us
tasks.question: Who owes us money right now, and how much?

queries.name: outstanding_by_customer
queries.sql: select c.customer_name, i.currency_code, count(*) as unpaid_invoices, round(sum(i.total_amt), 2) as amount_owed from finance.invoices i join sales.customers c on c.cust_id = i.cust_id where i.status in ('open', 'overdue') group by c.customer_name, i.currency_code order by amount_owed desc limit 20

tasks.name: overspent_budget_q2_2026
tasks.question: Are we bleeding money anywhere? Which parts of the business blew past their budget in Q2 2026?

queries.name: q2_2026_actual_vs_budget
queries.sql: with actual as (select g.cost_center_id, sum(g.debit_amt - g.credit_amt) as actual_amt from finance.gl_entries g join finance.chart_of_accounts a on a.gl_account_id = g.gl_account_id where a.account_type = 'expense' and g.entry_dt >= '2026-04-01' and g.entry_dt < '2026-07-01' group by g.cost_center_id), plan as (select b.cost_center_id, sum(b.budget_amt) as budget_amt from finance.budgets b join finance.chart_of_accounts a on a.gl_account_id = b.gl_account_id where a.account_type = 'expense' and b.fiscal_month >= '2026-04-01' and b.fiscal_month < '2026-07-01' group by b.cost_center_id) select cc.cc_code, cc.cc_name, round(coalesce(ac.actual_amt, 0), 2) as actual_amt, round(coalesce(p.budget_amt, 0), 2) as budget_amt, round(coalesce(ac.actual_amt, 0) - coalesce(p.budget_amt, 0), 2) as over_budget from finance.cost_centers cc left join actual ac on ac.cost_center_id = cc.cost_center_id left join plan p on p.cost_center_id = cc.cost_center_id order by over_budget desc limit 15

tasks.name: recurring_revenue_by_plan
tasks.question: How's our monthly recurring revenue split across the different plans?

queries.name: mrr_by_plan
queries.sql: select p.plan_name, count(*) as subscriptions, round(sum(s.mrr_amt), 2) as mrr_usd from finance.subscriptions s join finance.plans p on p.plan_id = s.plan_id where s.status in ('active', 'past_due') group by p.plan_name order by mrr_usd desc limit 10

tasks.name: why_subscribers_cancel
tasks.question: Why are customers cancelling their subscriptions?

queries.name: cancel_reasons
queries.sql: select cancel_reason, count(*) as cancellations, round(sum(mrr_amt), 2) as lost_mrr_usd from finance.subscriptions where status = 'cancelled' group by cancel_reason order by cancellations desc limit 10

tasks.name: failed_payments_sep_2026
tasks.question: How many customer payments bounced in September 2026, and how were they trying to pay?

queries.name: failed_payments_by_method
queries.sql: select method, count(*) as failed_payments, round(sum(amt), 2) as amount from finance.payments where status = 'failed' and paid_dt >= '2026-09-01' and paid_dt < '2026-10-01' group by method order by failed_payments desc limit 10

tasks.name: pipeline_worth
tasks.question: What's our sales pipeline worth right now?

queries.name: open_pipeline_by_stage
queries.sql: select stage, count(*) as deals, round(sum(amt), 2) as amount_usd, round(sum(amt * probability_pct / 100.0), 2) as weighted_usd from crm.opportunities where stage not in ('closed_won', 'closed_lost') group by stage order by amount_usd desc limit 10

tasks.name: why_we_lose_deals
tasks.question: Why do we keep losing deals?

queries.name: lost_reasons
queries.sql: select lost_reason, count(*) as lost_deals, round(sum(amt), 2) as lost_amount_usd from crm.opportunities where stage = 'closed_lost' group by lost_reason order by lost_deals desc limit 10

tasks.name: lead_sources_that_convert
tasks.question: Where do our best leads come from - which ones actually end up as customers?

queries.name: conversion_by_lead_source
queries.sql: select lead_source, count(*) as leads, count(converted_account_id) as converted, round(100.0 * count(converted_account_id) / count(*), 2) as conversion_pct from crm.leads group by lead_source order by conversion_pct desc limit 10

tasks.name: strategic_clients_gone_quiet
tasks.question: Which of our big strategic clients have gone quiet on us - nobody's talked to them in ages?

queries.name: stale_strategic_accounts
queries.sql: select a.account_id, a.account_name, max(act.activity_dt) as last_touch from crm.accounts a left join crm.activities act on act.account_id = a.account_id where a.tier = 'strategic' and a.is_active group by a.account_id, a.account_name order by last_touch asc nulls first limit 20

tasks.name: least_likely_to_recommend
tasks.question: Which clients would be least likely to recommend us to a friend?

queries.name: lowest_nps_accounts
queries.sql: select account_id, account_name, tier, nps_score, health_score from crm.accounts where nps_score is not null order by nps_score asc, health_score asc limit 20

tasks.name: tickets_sitting_open
tasks.question: Which support tickets have been sitting there unresolved the longest?

queries.name: oldest_unresolved_tickets
queries.sql: select ticket_ref, account_id, priority, status, opened_at from support.tickets where resolved_at is null and status not in ('resolved', 'closed') order by opened_at asc limit 20

tasks.name: missed_support_promises
tasks.question: How often are we missing our support response promises, broken down by support plan?

queries.name: breach_rate_by_tier
queries.sql: select tr.tier_name, count(distinct t.ticket_id) as tickets, count(distinct b.ticket_id) as breached_tickets, round(100.0 * count(distinct b.ticket_id) / count(distinct t.ticket_id), 2) as breach_pct from support.tickets t join support.tiers tr on tr.tier_id = t.tier_id left join support.sla_breaches b on b.ticket_id = t.ticket_id group by tr.tier_name order by breach_pct desc limit 10

tasks.name: fastest_support_people
tasks.question: Who on the support team sorts out problems the fastest?

queries.name: fastest_agents
queries.sql: select ag.agent_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, count(*) as resolved_tickets, round(avg(extract(epoch from (t.resolved_at - t.opened_at)) / 3600)::numeric, 1) as avg_hours from support.tickets t join support.agents ag on ag.agent_id = t.assigned_agent_id join hr.employees e on e.employee_id = ag.employee_id where t.resolved_at is not null group by ag.agent_id, e.first_name, e.last_name having count(*) >= 50 order by avg_hours asc limit 10

tasks.name: what_people_complain_about
tasks.question: What are customers complaining about the most?

queries.name: top_ticket_categories
queries.sql: select category, subcategory, count(*) as tickets from support.tickets group by category, subcategory order by tickets desc limit 15

tasks.name: support_satisfaction_trend
tasks.question: Are people getting happier or grumpier with our support over time?

queries.name: csat_by_month
queries.sql: select date_trunc('month', opened_at)::date as month, count(csat_score) as rated, round(avg(csat_score), 2) as avg_csat from support.tickets where csat_score is not null group by 1 order by 1 limit 40

tasks.name: leavers_2026
tasks.question: How many people left the company in 2026, and why did they go?

queries.name: leavers_by_reason_2026
queries.sql: select coalesce(termination_reason, '(none)') as reason, count(*) as leavers from hr.employees where term_dt >= '2026-01-01' and term_dt < '2026-10-11' group by 1 order by leavers desc limit 10

tasks.name: biggest_teams_by_manager
tasks.question: Which managers have the most people reporting to them?

queries.name: direct_report_counts
queries.sql: select m.employee_id, m.first_name, m.last_name, m.job_title, count(*) as direct_reports from hr.employees e join hr.employees m on m.employee_id = e.manager_id where e.is_active group by m.employee_id, m.first_name, m.last_name, m.job_title order by direct_reports desc limit 10

tasks.name: hoarding_vacation
tasks.question: Who's sitting on a mountain of unused vacation days?

queries.name: largest_pto_balances
queries.sql: select employee_id, first_name, last_name, job_title, pto_balance_days from hr.employees where is_active and pto_balance_days is not null order by pto_balance_days desc limit 20

tasks.name: top_performers_latest_review
tasks.question: Who were our standout performers in the most recent review round?

queries.name: top_rated_2026_h1
queries.sql: select e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, e.job_title, r.rating from hr.performance_reviews r join hr.employees e on e.employee_id = r.employee_id where r.review_period = '2026-H1' and r.rating is not null order by r.rating desc, e.employee_id limit 25

tasks.name: pending_time_off
tasks.question: Whose time-off requests are still waiting on a yes or no?

queries.name: pending_leave_requests
queries.sql: select t.request_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, t.leave_type, t.start_dt, t.end_dt, t.days, t.requested_at from hr.time_off t join hr.employees e on e.employee_id = t.employee_id where t.status = 'requested' order by t.requested_at asc limit 25

tasks.name: about_to_run_out
tasks.question: What are we about to run out of?

queries.name: below_reorder_point
queries.sql: select p.sku, p.product_name, s.warehouse_id, s.qty_on_hand - s.qty_reserved as available, s.reorder_point from inventory.stock_levels s join inventory.products p on p.product_id = s.product_id where s.qty_on_hand - s.qty_reserved < s.reorder_point order by (s.qty_on_hand - s.qty_reserved) - s.reorder_point asc limit 25

tasks.name: late_suppliers
tasks.question: Which of our suppliers are always late getting stuff to us?

queries.name: late_po_rate_by_supplier
queries.sql: select s.supplier_name, count(*) as received_pos, count(*) filter (where o.received_dt > o.expected_dt) as late_pos, round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where o.received_dt > o.expected_dt) / count(*), 1) as late_pct from ops.orders o join inventory.suppliers s on s.supplier_id = o.supplier_id where o.received_dt is not null group by s.supplier_name having count(*) >= 20 order by late_pct desc limit 15

tasks.name: slowest_shipping_company
tasks.question: Which shipping company takes the longest to get orders to people?

queries.name: avg_delivery_days_by_carrier
queries.sql: select c.carrier_name, count(*) as deliveries, round(avg(extract(epoch from (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 2) as avg_days from ops.shipments s join ops.carriers c on c.carrier_id = s.carrier_id where s.delivered_at is not null group by c.carrier_name order by avg_days desc limit 12

tasks.name: stock_of_dead_products
tasks.question: Are we sitting on stock for things we don't even sell anymore?

queries.name: stock_of_discontinued
queries.sql: select p.sku, p.product_name, p.discontinued_at, sum(s.qty_on_hand) as units_on_hand, round(sum(s.qty_on_hand * p.unit_cost), 2) as value_usd from inventory.products p join inventory.stock_levels s on s.product_id = p.product_id where (p.discontinued_at is not null or not p.is_active) and s.qty_on_hand > 0 group by p.sku, p.product_name, p.discontinued_at order by value_usd desc limit 20

tasks.name: deliveries_gone_sideways_oct_2026
tasks.question: How many deliveries went sideways in October 2026?

queries.name: shipment_exceptions_oct_2026
queries.sql: select shipped_at::date as ship_day, count(*) as problem_shipments from ops.shipments where status = 'exception' and shipped_at >= '2026-10-01' and shipped_at < '2026-11-01' group by 1 order by 1 limit 31

tasks.name: campaign_bang_for_buck
tasks.question: Which marketing campaigns gave us the most bang for our buck?

queries.name: cost_per_converted_lead
queries.sql: select c.campaign_name, c.channel, c.actual_spend_amt, count(l.lead_id) as leads, count(l.converted_account_id) as converted, round(c.actual_spend_amt / nullif(count(l.converted_account_id), 0), 2) as cost_per_conversion from marketing.campaigns c left join crm.leads l on l.campaign_id = c.campaign_id group by c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, c.channel, c.actual_spend_amt having count(l.converted_account_id) > 0 order by cost_per_conversion asc limit 15

tasks.name: anyone_opening_emails
tasks.question: Is anybody actually opening the marketing emails we send out?

queries.name: open_rate_by_campaign
queries.sql: select campaign_id, count(*) filter (where event_type = 'delivered') as delivered, count(*) filter (where event_type = 'open') as opens, round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where event_type = 'open') / nullif(count(*) filter (where event_type = 'delivered'), 0), 2) as open_pct from marketing.email_events group by campaign_id order by open_pct desc nulls last limit 20

tasks.name: web_traffic_sources
tasks.question: Where is our website traffic coming from, and does any of it actually buy?

queries.name: sessions_by_source
queries.sql: select coalesce(utm_source, '(direct)') as source, count(*) as sessions, count(*) filter (where converted) as conversions, round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where converted) / count(*), 2) as conversion_pct from analytics.web_sessions group by 1 order by sessions desc limit 15

tasks.name: features_customers_use
tasks.question: Which parts of our product are customers actually using?

queries.name: usage_by_feature
queries.sql: select feature_name, count(distinct account_id) as accounts, sum(event_count) as events from analytics.feature_usage group by feature_name order by events desc limit 20

tasks.name: fishy_logins_since_sep_2026
tasks.question: Anything fishy going on with people trying to log in since September 2026?

queries.name: failed_logins_by_user
queries.sql: select user_id, count(*) filter (where not success) as failed_attempts, count(*) as attempts, count(distinct ip_address) filter (where not success) as distinct_ips from ops.login_events where event_ts >= '2026-09-01' and event_ts < '2026-10-11' group by user_id order by failed_attempts desc limit 20

tasks.name: who_exports_or_deletes
tasks.question: Who's been pulling data out of the system or deleting things?

queries.name: exporters_and_deleters
queries.sql: select u.username, u.user_type, a.action, count(*) as events from public.audit_log a join ops.app_users u on u.user_id = a.actor_user_id where a.action in ('export', 'delete') group by u.username, u.user_type, a.action order by events desc limit 20

tasks.name: customer_integrations_erroring
tasks.question: Which customers' integrations with us keep erroring out?

queries.name: api_failures_by_account
queries.sql: select ac.account_name, count(*) as requests, count(*) filter (where r.status_code >= 400) as failed, round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where r.status_code >= 400) / count(*), 2) as fail_pct from ops.api_request_log r join ops.api_keys k on k.api_key_id = r.api_key_id join crm.accounts ac on ac.account_id = k.account_id group by ac.account_name order by failed desc limit 15

tasks.name: salary_changes_2026
tasks.question: Who's been changing people's pay in 2026?

queries.name: salary_edits_2026
queries.sql: select changed_by, change_source, count(*) as salary_changes, min(changed_at) as first_change, max(changed_at) as last_change from public.change_history where table_name = 'hr.employees' and column_name = 'salary_amt' and changed_at >= '2026-01-01' and changed_at < '2026-10-11' group by changed_by, change_source order by salary_changes desc limit 20

tasks.name: staff_without_2fa
tasks.question: Do we have any staff logging in without two-factor turned on?

queries.name: staff_no_mfa
queries.sql: select user_id, username, last_login_at, is_locked from ops.app_users where user_type = 'staff' and not mfa_enabled order by last_login_at desc nulls last limit 25

tasks.name: dead_keys_still_used
tasks.question: Are any API keys we already shut off still being used?

queries.name: calls_after_revocation
queries.sql: select k.api_key_id, k.key_name, k.revoked_at, count(*) as calls_after_revoke, max(r.requested_at) as last_call from ops.api_keys k join ops.api_request_log r on r.api_key_id = k.api_key_id where k.revoked_at is not null and r.requested_at > k.revoked_at group by k.api_key_id, k.key_name, k.revoked_at order by calls_after_revoke desc limit 20
